title: Database failover during commit: reconcile uncertain outcomes without duplicate effects
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Fail during commit; classify committed, failed, and unresolved outcomes without duplicating effects.
sourceAcceptance: Retries do not duplicate effects; committed, failed, and unresolved outcomes are attributed honestly.
preconditions: A modern browser opens local HTML, CSS and JavaScript; no server or account.
Three fixed synthetic operations each intend exactly one effect under a fixed original operation key and payload.
The fault loses all three commit acknowledgements; acknowledgement loss is not evidence of non-commit.
Reconciliation supplies an authoritative commit receipt, a terminal abort receipt and selected later evidence.
A terminal abort cannot later commit. A same-key retry after confirmed abort produces one effect and receipt in an assumed synthetic durable deduplication ledger.
Missing or unavailable lookup evidence cannot authorize a retry or establish an abort.
actions: Choose later evidence for SYN-663 and one bounded recovery policy.
Begin three commits, then inject failover before commit acknowledgements arrive.
Reconcile original committed, failed and unresolved outcomes from supplied receipts.
Apply recovery; inspect original and recovered attribution, effect bounds and duplicate counts.
Check a learning prediction separately from gate, user impact and cleanup.
Inspect retained proof, start a new attempt retaining history or explicitly reset all local memory.
assertions: Lost acknowledgements leave three unresolved outcomes before authoritative reconciliation.
Only terminal abort evidence classifies an original attempt as failed; missing lookup stays unresolved.
Safe recovery reuses committed receipts, retries confirmed aborts once with original keys and unchanged payloads, and holds unresolved operations.
Blind new-key retries duplicate a known committed effect; duplicate risk remains bounded but unresolved when evidence is unavailable.
Known missing or duplicate effects fail the gate; unresolved outcomes without a known failure yield UNKNOWN, never PASS.
Original failures and three interrupted commit responses remain visible even after all effects recover.
Strict inputs, ordered lifecycle, immutable detached snapshots and six-attempt retained history are guarded.

iac.decisionStage: After genuine behavioral RED and before behavior implementation
iac.reason: Resource-free local synthetic lesson; no cloud/IaC/scaffold/identity/deploy/spend.

testRuntime.purpose: Existing Node22 test tooling only; not production Node24 certification.

limits: Every operation, receipt, effect, fault and recovery result is deterministic synthetic data.
No actual database commit, transaction, durable deduplication, replication, concurrency or failover proof.
No real authentication, registration, credentials, Azure calls, IaC, deployment or expenditure.
A successful recovery gate or learning verifier does not erase the three interrupted commit responses or prove uninterrupted migration.
At most six attempts are retained in browser memory; explicit reset or reload clears history.
No production Node24, native platform, source-parent completion or five-nines certification.
The abandoned browser lifecycle prototype is unqualified; no unattended-runner certification.
B-S066 and the original D-S066 native acceptance remain separate and unfulfilled.
One frozen S unit; tests, evidence and refinement earn no additional units.
